channel.title: Tiny Interpreters
channel.description: Learn how programming languages work, one tiny interpreter at a time.

item.title: FUN: First-Class Functions, Currying, and a Surprise
item.description: Extend LET with first-class functions, then use currying and partial application to uncover an unexpected consequence of how function calls are evaluated.

item.title: LETDEP: Dependency-Ordered Binding Semantics for let Expressions
item.description: LETDEP gives multiple-binding let expressions dependency-ordered binding semantics: initializer dependencies determine the evaluation order, allowing forward references while rejecting duplicate names and cyclic bindings.

item.title: LETSEQ: Sequential Binding Semantics for let Expressions
item.description: LETSEQ gives multiple-binding let expressions sequential binding semantics: bindings are evaluated in source order, with each new binding becoming available to the ones that follow it.

item.title: LETPAR: Parallel Binding Semantics for let Expressions
item.description: LETPAR gives multiple-binding let expressions parallel binding semantics: every initializer is evaluated in the incoming environment, so sibling bindings cannot see one another.

item.title: Multiple-Binding let Expressions - Syntax Before Semantics
item.description: Extend LET so a single let expression can contain multiple bindings, updating the grammar, AST, and parser before deciding what those bindings mean.

item.title: LET: Introducing Local Bindings and Scope
item.description: LET extends VAR with let expressions, allowing programs to introduce local bindings and showing how environments determine their scope and support shadowing.

item.title: VAR: Variables and Environments
item.description: VAR extends IF with variable expressions and environments, making evaluation depend on context as variable names are looked up in the current environment.

item.title: IF: Conditional Expressions and Selective Evaluation
item.description: IF extends ZERO with conditional expressions, using Boolean conditions to choose which of two branches to evaluate while leaving the other unevaluated.

item.title: Make it a Syntax Error
item.description: See how grammar and AST design in a tiny Elm interpreter can turn runtime type errors into syntax errors, simplify evaluation, and connect to GADTs.

item.title: ZERO: Boolean Values and Runtime Type Errors
item.description: ZERO extends DIFF with the zero? predicate and Boolean values, then introduces runtime type errors for expressions that use values of the wrong type.

item.title: Simplifying Whitespace with Lexeme Parsers in Elm
item.description: Learn how lexeme parsers simplify whitespace handling in elm/parser by consuming trailing whitespace and keeping parsers close to the grammar.

item.title: Why Recursive Elm Parsers Need Parser.lazy
item.description: Learn why recursive Elm parsers create cyclic definitions, how Parser.lazy breaks the cycle, and when recursive parsers do and don't need it.

item.title: DIFF: When Expressions Contain Expressions
item.description: DIFF extends CONST with difference expressions whose operands are themselves expressions, revealing the same recursive structure in the grammar, AST, parser, and evaluator.

item.title: Setting Up a Reproducible Elm Interpreter Project with Nix
item.description: Set up a reproducible Elm interpreter project with a Nix flake, Elm tooling, helper commands, source and test structure, and grammar documentation.

item.title: Testing an Elm Interpreter with elm-test
item.description: Learn how to test an Elm interpreter with elm-test at the lexer, parser, and interpreter boundaries, then extract a reusable testValue helper.

item.title: CONST: From Source Text to Value
item.description: CONST is a tiny Elm interpreter for non-negative integer constants, showing the path from source text through an AST to an evaluated value.
